method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the definition, enumeration examples and computable-set inclusion proof, with exact formula, macro and identifier parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Computably enumerable sets, their historical recursively enumerable synonym, repetitions in enumeration and computable sets as a subclass.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A set is computably enumerable if it is empty or the range of a computable function. Recursively enumerable is the original alternate term; c.e. and r.e. are also in common use. If S is the range of f, the list f(0),f(1),... enumerates it, with neither increasing order nor injectivity required, so repeats are allowed; the constant zero function enumerates {0}.
samples.checks: The explicit empty-set clause, total computable function, historical terminology, both permitted nonmonotonicity and repetitions, and the constant example are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every computable set is computably enumerable. The empty case follows by definition; for nonempty S choose a in S and define f(x)=x when the characteristic function says x is in S, otherwise a. This total computable f has range exactly S.
samples.checks: The nonempty witness a, 1-membership case, fallback a, computability and exact range conclusion remain explicit.

source_observations: T327 deliberately distinguishes effective enumeration from ordinary countability: MR-P129 separates संगणनक्षम from गणनीय, while MR-P033 supports प्रगणन.
The English ordinary labels in the piecewise formula are translated into Marathi; all protected math tokens remain exact.
limitations: The full Marathi computably-enumerable compound is transparent and source-controlled but lacks direct headword attestation; it remains expert-reviewable.
